cover.alt: Wren zooms over Moss, Tansy and Puddle as they hold up a rock full of blue crystals

text: It was a sunny morning in Willowbrook Hollow.
Moss, Puddle and Tansy were down at the stream. Tansy was skipping stones. Plip, plip, plop!
Puddle was looking at a bug. Moss was looking at the reeds.
There was a rock in the reeds. It was round and gray and lumpy.
“That rock is odd,” said Moss.

media.alt: Moss peeks at a round, lumpy gray rock in the reeds while Tansy skips stones and Puddle watches a bug

text: “It is a rock,” said Tansy. “Rocks are not odd. Rocks are rocks.”
Moss gave it a poke. It did not go tunk, and it did not go thud. It went TONK!
“Rocks do not go tonk,” said Moss. “I think this one is empty inside.”
Puddle was still looking at the bug.

media.alt: Moss pokes the odd rock with a stick while Tansy shrugs and Puddle stares at a bug

text: Then the bug flew off, and Puddle went after it.
He did not look where he was going. He went back, back, back.
Bump! His tail hit the odd rock, and the rock began to roll.
It rolled down the bank, faster and faster.
It hit a big flat rock at the bottom.
CRACK!

media.alt: Puddle backs into the odd rock and it rolls down the bank toward a big flat rock

text: The odd rock split in two. Moss, Tansy and Puddle ran down to look.
Inside the rock, it was not gray. It was blue!
It was full of crystals. They were shiny, like tiny stars. They glinted in the sun.
“Oh,” said Moss. Then he rolled up into a ball.
That is what Moss does when a thing is too good.

media.alt: The rock lies split open, full of shiny blue crystals, while Tansy and Puddle gasp and Moss rolls into a ball

text: Tansy hopped up and down. “It is the best thing in the whole Hollow! We have to tell everyone!”
Then she stopped hopping. “Wait. Not Wren.”
Moss peeked out of his ball. “Why not Wren?”
“Wren tells it too big,” said Tansy. “A bug turns into a bear. A drip turns into a flood.”
She scratched a plan on a bit of bark.
“Step one: tell everyone. Step two: tell Wren last. Very, very last.”

media.alt: Tansy holds up a plan on bark next to the blue crystal rock while Moss peeks out of his ball

text: First, they went to the big oak. Brindle was asleep in his sunny spot.
Tansy held up the rock, and Brindle opened one eye. Then he opened the other eye.
“Well, well,” he said slowly. “Old dogs have seen many rocks. None of them had stars.”
“Do not tell Wren,” said Tansy.
“I will not,” said Brindle. “Old dogs are good at secrets. We nap before we tell.”

media.alt: Brindle opens his eyes under the big oak as Tansy holds up the crystal rock, with Moss and Puddle beside her

text: Next, they went to the log. Pip and Pebble ran out to see.
“It is blue,” said Pip.
“It is not blue,” said Pebble. “It is sky blue.”
“Sky blue IS blue!” said Pip.
“Do not tell Wren!” said Tansy.
“We will not,” said Pip and Pebble.
“I said it first,” said Pip.
“No, I did,” said Pebble.

media.alt: Pip and Pebble argue in front of their log while Tansy shows them the crystal rock

text: Echo was up on the gate, napping. Or he was acting like it.
“Echo, look!” said Tansy.
“A rock is just a rock, Nutty,” said Echo. But he sneaked a peek. Then a long look.
“Fine,” he said. “It is a very good rock. It would look great in my satchel.”
“No!” said Tansy. “And do not tell Wren!”
“Tell who?” said Echo. “I am napping.”

media.alt: Echo lies on the gate pretending to nap while peeking at the crystal rock Tansy holds up

text: Leo was on the hill, munching grass. He held his wish ball up next to the crystals. Blue and blue. Glow and glow.
“Hey!” said Leo. “What did the big rock say to the little rock?”
Moss knew this one. Everyone knew this one.
“Nothing!” said Leo. “Rocks can’t talk!” He laughed so hard he fell over.
“Do not tell Wren,” said Tansy.
“Rocks can’t talk,” said Leo, “and Leo can’t tell!”

media.alt: Leo holds his glowing blue wish ball next to the glowing blue crystals while Moss, Tansy and Puddle watch

text: The parrots were at their gold tree. June and Johnafur looked at the rock.
“A rock with stars, a rock of blue!” said June.
“We will not tell, we promise you!” said Johnafur.
Juneafur blew a bubble. “A wock! A wock!” she said. Pop!
“Not a peep to Wren from us!” sang June and Johnafur.
“Not a peep, and not a fuss!”

media.alt: The parrot family admires the crystal rock by their gold tree while Juneafur blows bubbles

text: By lunch, everyone in the Hollow knew about the rock.
Brindle knew, and Pip and Pebble knew. Echo knew, Leo knew, and the parrots knew.
Everyone knew but one small bird.
“Step one is done,” said Tansy. “Now for step two.”
Moss looked up at the trees. “Wren will be so happy,” he said.
Tansy was not so sure.

media.alt: Moss, Tansy and Puddle walk back with the crystal rock, and Moss looks up at the trees

text: Wren was up in a tree, singing a song about a cloud.
“Wren!” said Tansy. “We have news!”
Wren zipped down so fast she did a flip.
“News? I LOVE news! News is my best thing!”
“What is it? Is it big? Is it huge? Tell me, tell me, tell me!”

media.alt: Wren zips down from a tree with a flip toward Moss, Tansy and Puddle

text: Moss held up the rock. The crystals glinted in the sun.
Wren’s eyes went very round. Her beak went very open.
“Oh my feathers,” she said. “Who else knows?”
Tansy looked at Moss, and Moss looked at Puddle. Puddle looked at a leaf.
“Um,” said Tansy. “Well…”

media.alt: Wren stares wide-eyed at the crystal rock Moss holds up while Tansy and Puddle look away

text: But Wren did not wait. “Hold on!” she sang. “This is BREAKING NEWS!”
And off she went. Zip, zoom, up and away.
“Wait!” said Tansy. “Wren! They all—”
But Wren was long gone.
Moss sat down on the bank. “Uh oh,” he said. “I think the plan just got a lot bigger.”
Puddle was still looking at the leaf.

media.alt: Wren zooms away over the hill while Tansy calls after her and Moss sits down on the bank

text: Wren landed on the big oak, just over Brindle’s nose.
“BREAKING NEWS! BREAKING NEWS!”
Brindle opened one sleepy eye and looked at her.
“Moss found a rock!” said Wren. “And it is full of stars!”
“I know,” said Brindle.
Wren blinked. “You know about the rock?”
“I know,” said Brindle, and he shut his eye again.

media.alt: Wren shouts her news at Brindle, who opens one sleepy eye under the big oak

text: Wren zipped over to the log by the stream.
“BREAKING NEWS! The rock is as big as a barn!”
“No, it is not,” said Pip. “It is as big as a duck.”
“It is as big as a hat,” said Pebble.
“A duck in a hat,” said Pip, and they both nodded.
“We know,” said Pip and Pebble. “We saw it.”
Wren’s feathers drooped, just a bit.

media.alt: Wren spreads her news at the log while Pip and Pebble shrug

text: Wren zipped over to the gate, as fast as she could.
“BREAKING NEWS! A duck made the rock! With his feet!”
Echo did not open his eyes. “Old news, Beaky.”
“But I made up the duck part!” said Wren.
“Still old,” said Echo, and he went on napping.

media.alt: Wren yells at Echo on the gate, and Echo keeps his eyes shut

text: Wren zipped up the hill to find Leo.
“BREAKING NEWS! The rock can TALK!”
Leo sat up. “Rocks can’t talk!” he said. “That is my joke!”
“Is it old news too?” asked Wren.
“Very old,” said Leo. “I tell it each day.”

media.alt: Wren tells her news to Leo on the hill, and Leo sits up grinning

text: Wren zipped to the gold tree. “BREAKING—”
“Old news, old news, we know it too!” sang June and Johnafur.
“The rock is gray, the stars are blue!”
Juneafur blew a bubble at Wren. Pop!
“Old news!” said Juneafur.
Wren sat down on a twig, and she did not sing.

media.alt: The parrot family sings back at Wren by the gold tree while a bubble pops on her beak

text: Then Wren saw the giant. It was Zoe, with her feed bucket.
Wren had one last try. “BREAKING NEWS!” she sang. “Moss found a rock full of stars!”
Zoe grinned. “What a pretty song, little bird,” she said.
“At last!” said Wren. “Someone who did not know!”
Zoe hummed and went on her way. She did not know one bit of it.

media.alt: Wren sings her news to Zoe, who smiles down at her with a feed bucket

text: Wren went back to the stream. She sat on a reed and looked at her feet.
Moss sat next to her. He did not talk at first. Moss never talks at first.
“We told you last,” he said at last. “Because you tell it so big.”
“Big is the best part,” said Wren, very small.

media.alt: Wren sits sadly on a reed by the stream as Moss sits down next to her

text: “And last is the worst part,” said Wren. “When you are last, there is no one left to tell.”
Tansy looked at her plan. “Hmm,” she said. “Step two was a bad step.”
Moss nodded. “Next time, you can be first.”
Wren sniffed. “There will not be a next time. Rocks with stars do not come in twos.”

media.alt: Tansy frowns at her plan while Moss and Wren sit by the stream

text: Then Puddle stood up. He had been looking at a leaf this whole time.
And he had been sitting on something. Something round. Something gray. Something lumpy.
Wren looked at it. Wren looked at Puddle. Her feathers stood up.
“BREAKING NEWS!” she sang. “Puddle was sitting on a SECOND ONE!”
“I was?” said Puddle, and he looked down at it.

media.alt: Puddle stands up to show a second lumpy rock under him, and Wren puffs up with excitement

text: “We did NOT know that!” said Moss and Tansy.
Wren puffed up so big, she was round.
“Then it is REAL news! First news! Best news!”
Off she zipped to tell the whole Hollow.
And this time, not one friend said, “We know.”
They all ran to the stream to see.

media.alt: Wren zooms off over the Hollow, and her friends run toward the stream

text: Puddle gave the rock a bump. CRACK!
Inside, the crystals were pink.
“Breaking news,” said Wren. “This one is as big as a BARN!”
It was as big as an acorn. A small one.
Everyone laughed, and Wren laughed the most of all.

media.alt: The whole Hollow gathers around a tiny rock split open with pink crystals, and everyone laughs
